subject: Mutual action plan / security gates for ApexTrust evaluation
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Weber <tom.weber@apextrust.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action plan / security gates for ApexTrust evaluation

Tom — thanks again for the thoughtful demo yesterday. As promised, I’m putting a short MAP here focused on the security/compliance milestones we need to clear for an evaluation-to-production decision. We want to keep the timeline tight but realistic so your teams can plan procurement and integration windows.

Summary / proposed milestones (high level)
- Week 0 (this week): Exchange SOC 2 report + CAIQ/SIG snapshot. Legal to review initial DPA carveouts.
- Week 1: Security intake workshop — walkthrough of data flows, residency, and retention buckets.
- Week 2: Evidence collection window — our team to provide sample logs, architecture diagrams, and perf baseline notes.
- Week 3: Finalize DPA redlines and obtain signatures (DocuSign).
- Week 4: Acceptance run — test tenant + latency/cost baseline; signoff on SOC 2/CAIQ items or agreed mitigations.

Asks from ApexTrust before the intake workshop:
1) Current SOC 2 report (if recent) or the auditor point-of-contact so we can map gaps.
2) CAIQ/SIG answers you have on file (we can provide a template to accelerate).
3) Any non-standard retention/ residency constraints (EU-only data, escrow requirements, etc.).

We’ve attached a 1-page MAP template and a draft DPA with common carveouts for financial services — not final, just a starting point. I’ve looped Ben (Sales) and Marissa (Security ops lead) to help run the intake and evidence collection. If this looks good, we’ll schedule the 60-minute intake workshop early next week.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Evals, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachments: MAP-template-1p.pdf (stub), DPA-draft-ApexTrust-20260914.docx (stub)

From: Tom Weber <tom.weber@apextrust.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal <legal@apextrust.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan / security gates for ApexTrust evaluation

Naomi — thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side before the workshop:

- SOC 2: We completed a Type II engagement in June 2026. I’ll attach the report; legal prefers we route any auditor-questions through our external counsel.
- CAIQ/SIG: We maintain a filled CAIQ for platform vendors; I’ll send our current answers. We do have two control items of concern: cross-region KV replication and third-party logging retention beyond 90 days.
- DPA: Our legal team flagged two asks — (1) a 7-year archival requirement for certain settlement-related records, and (2) EU residency for customer PII where the account is EU-based.

We’re keen to keep the timeline but need to ensure scope on the retention asks is practical. Workshop on Wednesday 09/16 at 11:00 PT works for us — does that fit your calendar?

Tom Weber
Head of Risk & Compliance, ApexTrust
Tom.Weber@apextrust.com

Attachment: SOC2-report-2026.pdf (stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Weber <tom.weber@apextrust.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, ApexTrust Legal <legal@apextrust.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan / security gates for ApexTrust evaluation

Tom — appreciate the fast turnaround and the SOC 2. Confirmed for the workshop: Wednesday 09/16, 11:00 PT. Agenda (60 minutes):
- 0–10m: Introductions & scope confirmation (Naomi / Tom).
- 10–25m: Data flow and residency map (Marissa to lead).
- 25–40m: Retention requirements deep-dive — which objects need 7-year archival vs 90-day logs (Ben to capture).
- 40–55m: CAIQ items + mitigation proposals for KV replication.
- 55–60m: Actions, owners, and target dates (DocuSign link + evidence list).

Pre-work for ApexTrust (helps to keep the workshop productive):
- Mark which datasets require 7-year archival and provide the names of the tables/streams.
- Share the CAIQ PDF and any live auditor contact (we'll respect counsel channeling).

Internal notes / owners:
- Marissa Cole: lead the intake + evidence checklist (architecture diagrams, network zones, KV replication config, logging retention indexes).
- Ben Carter: procurement cadence + DPA redline coordination; will track DocuSign milestone.

We’ll circulate the calendar invite with the workshop deck and an initial evidence checklist after this email. If Legal from your side wants to propose a narrow amendment for archival scoped to settlement records only, we can likely accept that with appropriate escrow/archival controls.

Thanks — see you Wednesday.
Naomi

Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2c3D_example_map_docs

From: Tom Weber <tom.weber@apextrust.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ApexTrust Legal <legal@apextrust.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan / security gates for ApexTrust evaluation

All — quick follow after the workshop. Appreciated the clarity from Marissa and Ben; our legal team prepared a short DPA redline that narrows the 7-year archival to: settlement transaction records tied to cleared trades only (we included definitions). They also requested a small amendment for EU PII residency: allow for EU-only customer accounts to be pinned to EU-hosted deployment (we understand there may be price/ops implications).

Next steps we propose:
- 09/18: ApexTrust legal to upload DPA redline to DocuSign (we’ll tag Ben as the signing contact).
- 09/20–09/24: Evidence drop window — ApexTrust uploads CAIQ + table list; Redwood provides KV replication design and retention policy samples.
- 09/25: Final DPA signature target.
- 09/30–10/04: Acceptance run in test tenant and latency baseline measurement.

We’re comfortable with that cadence pending Ben’s procurement check. Thanks — Tom
